clue.text: Beginning to sail across the Atlantic or Channel

indicators.note: the beginning of the word sail is its opening letter

parts.note: from Britain, across the Atlantic means in the US

explanation.surface: A sailor sets out to cross either the ocean or the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like the English Channel, a partner to 'the Atlantic'; it is the definition, a passage in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically a sinus is a cavity or passage, such as the channels behind the nose.

clue.text: Group quiet during drinks? They'll want a port

indicators.note: during places these inside the drinks

parts.note: sips are small drinks
a group or side is a team
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A team keeps quiet over drinks, hoping for a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' reads as the fortified wine after 'drinks'; it means a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean-going vessels need a harbour to dock in at the end of a voyage.

clue.text: Head teachers

definitions.meaning: the National Union of Teachers is a British trade union

explanation.surface: A head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The head is slangily a nut, and Britain's main teachers' union went by these initials.

clue.text: Alcohol ingested by British and yobs

indicators.note: ingested by says the answer is swallowed within British and yobs

explanation.surface: Drink is swallowed by Britons and louts alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer mixed with lemonade is a weak alcoholic drink popular in Britain.

clue.text: The present day has its charms, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of its charms may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Today, the present moment, has its own charms, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present day' reads as 'today'; it really means the day for giving presents.
explanation.definitionFit: December 25th is the day gifts are exchanged, so it is the day of presents.

clue.text: Sign of problem for walker south of island

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of puts the walker's problem below the island

parts.note: Capri is an island off Naples
a corn is a painful patch on the foot

explanation.surface: A hiker on an island signals foot trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Bones from arm and tibia with odd parts dislodged

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters of arm and tibia knocked out, only the even ones are left

explanation.surface: Bones from the arm and leg get partly dislocated.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; the clue's plural is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Sweet talker from Soho with time for frolicking

indicators.note: frolicking means playing about, so the letters of Soho and time are played with

explanation.surface: A smooth charmer from Soho, London's nightlife district, out for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, ingratiating person who talks persuasively is a smooth operator.

clue.text: Fear getting taken in by boring magician's trick

indicators.note: getting taken in by puts the fear inside the boring

parts.note: mining is boring into the ground
dread is fear

explanation.surface: A dull conjuror's act makes the audience fear being fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull; it is drilling, mining.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage mentalists claim to know a volunteer's thoughts as an illusion.

clue.text: Tender love directed heavenwards

indicators.note: in a down answer, directed heavenwards means the word is written upwards

parts.note: Eros is the god of love

explanation.surface: Gentle love aimed up to the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like gentle; it means painful.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise that is tender hurts to the touch.

clue.text: Maybe framed paintings returned before degree course in design

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: a design is an aim or purpose, an end

indicators.note: before places the paintings piece ahead of the degree course
returned says the word for paintings is read backwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art
PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: Pictures in frames sent back before a design student's course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks framed as one example of being caught, and 'degree course' is the British Oxford degree in Philosophy, Politics and Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone framed for a crime has been set up and caught by a trick, which is an instance of being snared.

clue.text: Days off a depressing experience for landlord

indicators.note: off says the letter for days is taken away

parts.note: a downer is something that depresses you
D is the standard abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: A landlord finds days off rather depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes D from DOWNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord is the proprietor of a property, the person holding title to it.

clue.text: Transport dilemma: trains run the wrong way

indicators.note: to transport is to carry away, so the letters of dilemma trains are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: A transport chief faces a dilemma: the trains are running in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage an organisation badly or dishonestly is to run it the wrong way.

clue.text: Departure of a doctor involved in disclosing secrets

indicators.note: involved in places these inside the leaking

parts.note: leaking is passing secrets on
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's departure follows involvement in leaking secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying farewell before going is a formal leave-taking, so a parting.

clue.text: Printer from ancient port mostly keeping seat in church ceremony

indicators.note: keeping says the port holds the rest inside it
mostly says the last letter of the port is dropped

parts.note: Tyre was a Phoenician port
a pew is a church seat
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A printer from an old port took a seat at church.
explanation.walkthrough: TYR, the port cut short by 'mostly', holds PEW and RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter prints letters onto paper, once the office printer.

clue.text: Try hard to get attention

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Someone strains to catch another person's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt'; here it is the legal sense, to judge a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who tries a case listens to it in court; to try and to hear are legal synonyms.

clue.text: Cops in novel with risque plot

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of cops in are made new

parts.note: risque means racy, slightly indecent

explanation.surface: A police story in a novel with a saucy storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' reads as a novel's storyline; it is a secret scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot in the sense of a secret scheme by several people is a synonym.

clue.text: Mocking actors wearing dress and cape

indicators.note: wearing puts the actors inside the dress

parts.note: a sari is an Indian dress
the actors in a play are the cast
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Actors in dresses and capes are being made fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneering, ironic mockery is the sarcastic tone.

clue.text: Pair of dopes heading for insolvency name liquidator

indicators.note: pair of says the word for a dope comes twice

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: heading for means the opening letter of insolvency

explanation.surface: Two idiots, heading for bankruptcy, name a liquidator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquidator' looks like a bankruptcy official; here it means someone who liquidates, a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate is slang for to kill, so a liquidator is a killer.

clue.text: Sally's last in school in hard-working class

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the class of workers

parts.note: the peasantry is the class of agricultural labourers

indicators.note: last in school is the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: Sally, the last in her school, belongs to a hard-working class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name; it is a witty remark. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a witty or jocular remark, as is a pleasantry.

clue.text: Audible expressions of frustration in mass

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard, not written

parts.note: sighs express frustration

explanation.surface: Groans of frustration are heard throughout a church mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like a church service; it means bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass and magnitude are near synonyms for how big something is.

clue.text: Party admitting blunder after raising VAT?

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising means the whole is written upwards
admitting puts the blunder inside the party

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A political party admits a mistake after putting up value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'VAT' looks like the British value added tax; it is a cask. 'raising' turns LERRAB upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tub or cask for liquid, as is a barrel.

clue.text: Carol's maturity and right clothing entrance a fellow

indicators.note: and joins the letters for maturity and right
clothing says those letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: maturity is age
an entrance is a way in
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Carol, grown up and right, dresses up the entrance for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is a Christmas song. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christmas hymn about the infant Jesus in a stable.

clue.text: Imbecile's docked marks, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: docked says the tail of the word is cut off

parts.note: an imbecile is an idiot; the 's means is
M is short for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A fool loses marks, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a way of expressing things characteristic of a language or speaker.

clue.text: Curse what an anti-drug law may do

definitions.meaning: a curse is a source of ruin or misery

definitions.text: what an anti-drug law may do
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a law may ban ecstasy, E

explanation.surface: A curse on drug laws.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse and a scourge are both sources of persistent trouble.

clue.text: Notice vast round island is so long

indicators.note: round says these go around the island letter

parts.note: a notice in a paper is an ad
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Spotting a huge round island, someone says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the island's shape, but it is the containment signal; 'vast' stands for outsize, the clothing-size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is a casual goodbye, as is the Spanish farewell.

clue.text: Cross from wing going behind Italian footballers

indicators.note: going behind places the wing after the footballers

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
a wing of a party or church is a faction, a sect

explanation.surface: A cross comes in from the wing behind the Italian defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' and 'wing' look like football; cross is a verb, and wing is a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lines that cross each other meet and pass through at a point.

clue.text: City bank dismissing its leader

indicators.note: dismissing its leader drops the opening letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A city bank sacks its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a small English cathedral city, so a city by status.

clue.text: Thus Mike welcomes working using biotechnology

indicators.note: welcomes says the working letters are taken inside

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
a machine that is working is on
a mike is a microphone, spelt mic

explanation.surface: So Mike takes on work in biotech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a man's name; it is a microphone. The working letters sit inside 'Thus' rather than inside Mike's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Biotechnology is an older, chiefly American name for the study of workplace design for human efficiency.

clue.text: Early shot in film

indicators.note: shot means broken up, so the letters of early are scrambled

explanation.surface: An early scene was shot in the movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie; it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A film of dust is a thin coating or stratum over a surface.
